fresh flow down the left half of the frame from crown to root-line, running off the top and bottom edges, a bulging leading edge as deep as a cone is long still moving, its top skin already wrinkling and matte over a body that is wet and mirror-bright pale honey, greenish-clear at the thin margins, one trapped bubble the size of a grape stopped halfway down its face

fresh flow in the lower-left corner running off the left and bottom edges, a thick slow tongue as deep as a cone is long at its leading edge, the top skin wrinkling into fine parallel ridges where it has begun to set, the body beneath mirror-bright pale honey, greenish-clear where it thins at the sides, a crack in the setting skin that has healed with a paler seam across its centre

hardened boulder sunk into the forest floor at the foot of a trunk, moss creeping up one flank and litter drifted against the other, centre-bottom and running off the bottom edge, as big as a resting animal, its outer crust dull and matte with grit and needle fragments pressed into it, cloudy inside with white cracks showing through, a plate of bark sealed just under the surface

stretched thread from a high branch filling the right third and running off the top and bottom edges, a single long strand the width of a horsetail stem, taut under the weight of its own hanging drop, nearly transparent pale honey, the drop at the bottom fat and mirror-bright and still pulling the strand a little longer, a grain of dark grit sealed inside the drop at its equator

bead row under a branch in the upper-right corner running off the top and right edges, the drops scattered at no regular interval along it, three crowded together at one knot and a long bare stretch beyond them, the smallest the size of a pea and the largest nearly the size of a walnut, all wet and mirror-bright, pale honey shading to dark treacle at the largest, one drop showing a single conifer needle pressed flat against its surface from the inside

torn scar filling the centre and upper-left running off the top and left edges, a wide ragged split in the trunk, the old crust on either side dark and pitted with old dried drips, fresh resin pouring through in a broad bright tongue, mirror-wet, pale honey at the surface, dark treacle in the depth of the wound where it is thickest, a run already beginning to skin at its lower lip

Hardened boulder swelling out of a trunk base and sunk into the needle-litter, the size of a crouching mid-weight animal, its outer crust dulled to an opaque milky tan and crazed all over with a network of shallow internal cracks, litter banked hard against its left flank and a twig pressed into the damp underside where it meets the floor, dark treacle at the dense core shading to cloudy rust where bark fragments are locked inside it, one corner gone entirely opaque white as old frost, filling the lower-right third and running off the right edge and the bottom

Stretched thread hanging from a low branch, a single long taut strand as thick as a cone's central spike drawn out nearly the full height of the frame, the top still attached to a dark smear of older resin on the bark, the bottom weighted by a drop the size of a large round seed still trembling with its own surface tension, the strand itself clear pale honey, the drop below clouded slightly where it has been gathering dust, running down the right third of the frame and just clearing the bottom edge without detaching

Bead row along the underside of a leaning branch crossing the upper half of the frame, individual drops at wildly uneven spacing — three crowded so close their shoulders nearly touch on the left, then a long bare gap, then one enormous drop the size of a small egg hanging alone, then two small tight ones, then nothing — each drop a round pale-honey lens with a bright point of reflected canopy light off its lowest curve, the branch itself dark and rough above them, running across the upper third and off both side edges

Lopsided accumulation on the right flank of a trunk where old flows landed at no regular interval, three uneven lobes of very different sizes piled against each other — the lowest and largest a cloudy rust-brown mass the size of a fern's root ball, the middle lobe smaller and tilted left and darker, the topmost a small fresh-looking pale honey knob off to the right of the others — none of them level or centred on the same axis, needles pressed into all outer surfaces, filling the right half of the frame and running off the right edge

Split nodule lying against a root on the forest floor, the outside a dull rough lump the size of a large pinecone, crust gone pale and cracked and stuck with old grit and a shred of bark, the freshly broken face exposed upward water-clear and smooth, showing the clean pale-honey interior with one small dark particle suspended inside it near the centre, the crack not straight but following an old internal seam, litter banked against the back of it and a dried needle lying across the broken face, sitting in the lower-left quarter and running off the left edge and the bottom

Glazed flank where the whole right face of a broad trunk is one continuous smooth coat of resin, wet-looking and mirror-bright from root-flare to the height of a large fern's full spread, thicker and darker at the base where it pooled before skinning, thinning to a near-clear glaze at the upper edge, pale honey overall with a dark treacle streak down the centre where the bark's ridge channelled extra flow, a single long needle caught vertically in the surface with its tip still free and trembling, the glazed face filling the right half of the frame and running off the right edge and both the top and bottom

Fresh flow welded to the upper surface of a reaching root, pooling in the root's curve before spilling over the outer edge in one thick slow tongue as long as a mid-sized cone, the leading edge a taut bulging meniscus still rounding downward, the upper surface already developing a faint wrinkling skin while the edges stay wet and bright, pale honey throughout with a slightly darker core where it is thickest, a tiny bubble stopped just below the surface skin halfway along the tongue, sitting in the lower-left quarter and running off the left edge and the bottom

Hanging sheet bridging the gap between a trunk and a close-leaning snag, roughly two fern-fronds wide, its surface matte on the outer face and catching diffuse daylight evenly, a heavy uneven lower roll that hangs noticeably lower on the left side where extra material gathered, the interior thick enough to turn the bark behind it into a vague dark shape, milky where old and clear pale honey at the lower roll where it is freshest, a small dead insect of the Cretaceous held inside the left side of the sheet, spanning the upper centre and running off the top and both side edges

Hardened boulder welded to the base of a large trunk, half-buried in needle-litter on its lower half, as wide as a large cycad trunk is thick, its outer crust a uniform dusty pale tan crazed into irregular sections by a network of surface cracks, dark treacle in the dense core seen dimly through the clouded crust, rust-brown where a band of bark is suspended inside the upper left, a crack running from the top that has healed with a paler opaque seam through it, filling the lower-centre and running off the bottom edge

Torn scar in the upper-left of the frame, the old crust dark and granular and split open in a rough mouth, fresh resin welling out bright and wet and greenish-clear only through the lower part of the breach, the new material beginning a slow run that has already moved the length of a large cone downward along the left side of the scar, sticky surface pulling thin threads where the flow separated from the crust edge, a needle stuck upright in the fresh dome, running off the left edge and the top

Lopsided accumulation on the underside of a jutting root-knee, three lobes of mismatched size grown at different seasons — a large old cloudy treacle-dark lobe on the right, a mid-sized pale honey lobe slumped left and lower, a small fresh pale knob attached to the upper left of the cluster at an awkward angle — none of them sharing a common centre of gravity, grit and bark fragments pressed into all outer surfaces, a dried needle draped over the right lobe, filling the upper-right corner and running off the right edge and the top

Pool spread on the forest floor at the downhill base of a trunk, as wide as a large fern's root spread, skinned over and matte, the skin holding a dozen fallen needles lying at all angles and a light scatter of pale grit, pale honey at the outer rim where it thinned, dark treacle at the centre where it is deepest, the uphill edge thicker and crinkled where the flow stalled before spreading flat, a small fern shoot emerging through the needle-litter beside the pool's right edge, filling the lower half and running off the bottom and left edges

Glazed flank covering the full left face of a narrow trunk from the root-flare to above the height of a large cycad's crown, the surface wet-looking and mirror-bright, thickest at the base where a slow surplus pooled before setting, thinning upward to a near-clear film, pale honey overall going to dark treacle in the pooled base section, the bark's grain visible as a ghostly texture under the clear upper portion, a single dead-bark flake stuck to the bright surface near the midpoint, the glazed flank filling the left half and running off the left edge and top and bottom

Glazed flank wrapping around the forward-left face of a trunk in one smooth continuous wet-looking coat, mirror-bright from the upper frame edge to where it thickens at the base, the coat as tall as four cones laid end-to-end, pale honey thinning at the margins toward the bark texture and deepening to dark treacle in the thick lower zone, the coat split around a protruding knot and rejoined below it with a faint raised seam, two needles pressed flat into the thickest lower zone, the glazed face filling the left half of the frame and running off the top, left, and bottom edges.
Hanging sheet between two leaning trunks, uneven in thickness — very thick and near

Hardened boulder welded to the base of a trunk, half-buried in the needle-litter with moss already creeping up its shadowed flank, as large as a crouching small animal, its outside surface dulled with dust and pressed grit, the whole mass crazed with a dense network of internal cracks that scatter light into a cloudy white interior, milky near the core and rust-coloured where bark is suspended in one thick lower lobe, filling the lower-right corner and running off the right and bottom edges.

Bead row welded to the underside of a leaning branch, drops at wildly uneven spacing — three crowded almost touching on the left, then a long bare gap, then one enormous drop the size of a cycad nut hanging alone, then two small tight ones near the right end — each a tiny round lens of pale honey, wet and mirror-bright on the bottom curve, matte and slightly skinned on top where it meets the bark, a single needle stuck to the largest drop's wet face, the branch crossing the upper third of the frame and running off both side edges.

Torn scar on a trunk face, the old crust dark and chewed-open along an uneven gash, the fresh resin welling out bright and wet through the centre of the wound in a slow bulging upwelling, pale honey at the wet core shading outward to dark treacle where the old crust is thick, the crust surface dull and pitted, the fresh face mirror-bright and sticky, a twig from the litter pressed flat against the lower wet edge, the scar running across the full right half of the frame from mid-height down and off the bottom edge.

Lopsided accumulation swelling out of the bark where three old flows have piled onto each other at no regular interval, the leftmost lobe the largest by far — roughly the size of a frond-head — the middle lobe half that size and pitched slightly downward, the rightmost a small knob set higher than either, no two lobes the same clarity: the big left lobe milky and crazed, the middle one dark treacle, the small right knob greenish-clear, all three surfaces dusted with needles and grit, banked litter pressed against the bottom, filling the left half of the frame and running off the left edge.

Hanging sheet swelling between two close trunks, a heavy sagging curtain barely half a trunk-width across but enormously thick — as deep as a cone is long — its bottom edge rolled into a fat uneven cord that droops lower on the left than the right, the whole mass pale honey at the top shading to near-black in the rolled lower cord, blurring the fern stems behind it into pale smears, grit caught along the upper edge where the sheet meets the bark, the sheet filling the upper-left quarter and running off the left and top edges.

Hardened boulder welded to a trunk base, a mass the size of a crouching lizard, its outer crust dulled with dust and embedded grit, crazed with cracks that run in all directions and split apart at one corner into a wide dark fissure, milky and opaque through most of its interior, one corner gone opaque white like frost, rust-coloured where a strip of bark is suspended in the lower lobe, a fern stem growing up past its right flank, the boulder filling the lower-left corner and running off the left and bottom edges.

Stretched thread hanging from the underside of a broken branch stub, a single long taut strand frozen in descent, clear as still water and mirror-bright along its full length which spans the height of a large fern frond, its lower end thickening into a heavy teardrop the size of a conifer bud still hanging motionless, the strand catching a line of flat light that traces its full curve, crossing the left quarter of the frame and running off the top and bottom edges.

Torn scar on a trunk, a ragged gash where the old crust has split along a vertical line, the crust surface dark and matte and pitted, the fresh resin welling up through the split in a slow bright upwelling that spills further down the right side than the left, pale honey at the fresh wet core, darkening to near-black at the old crust edges, the fresh surface mirror-bright and pulling a thin thread where a piece of litter barely touched it and swung free, the scar filling the centre of the frame from top to bottom and running off the top and bottom edges.

Lopsided accumulation on a trunk face, four old flows piled at no regular interval: the lowest and biggest a fat pale-honey lobe the size of a frond-head, above it on the right a dark treacle lobe half the size pitched at a downward angle, above that on the left a small cloudy knob, and highest of all a thin greenish-clear drip-tail hanging from the right edge of the second lobe, the whole pile surface dusted with needles and grit, a twig pressed into the bottom lobe's damp underside, the accumulation filling the right half of the frame and running off the right edge.

Pool on the litter where a heavy flow ran off a root and spread flat, covering an area roughly as wide as a large fern frond is long, its surface a dull matte skin with fine litter needles pressed flat into it, the near edge slightly tacky and pulling a thin thread where a fern tip rested and lifted, pale honey in the thin outer ring shading to dark treacle where it is deepest at the far edge against a root, the pool filling the lower-left corner and running off the left and bottom edges.

Split nodule half-buried in the litter against the base of a small root, its outer surface a dull cracked rust-coloured crust the size of a large seed-pod, needles pressed into the crust across its top, the freshly fractured inner face catching daylight and showing water-clear resin with a crack that has healed in one place with a paler seam running diagonally across the clear face, the nodule sitting in the lower-right of the frame with litter banked against it on both sides.

Glazed flank covering the whole shadowed side of a trunk, a smooth unbroken coat that runs from the root flare upward for the height a small theropod could reach, wet-looking and mirror-bright, greenish-clear at the thin upper margin, pale honey through the middle, pooling to dark treacle at the lowest point where it laps the root, a run that split around a bark ridge on the left and rejoined lower down leaving a dry patch inside, the glazed face filling the entire left half of the frame and running off the left, top, and bottom edges.

Fresh flow still moving on a bark face pitched at a slight angle, a thick heavy tongue the width of a large frond-stalk and deep as a cone is long, its leading edge a fat bulging lip creeping downward, the top skin matte and wrinkled while the underside is mirror-bright, pale honey shading to dark treacle where it is thickest, a crack in the wrinkling skin on the upper left that has sealed itself with a paler seam, the flow filling the lower-right third and running off the right and bottom edges.

Hardened boulder swelling out of the needle-litter at a trunk base, a mass as large as a crouching broad-bodied tortoise, its outer crust chalky and dull and embedded with grit and one pressed needle standing upright from the surface, crazed with internal cracks that go cloudy white in all directions from the centre, rust-coloured near the bottom where the oldest material is darkest, the boulder filling the lower-right quadrant and running off the right and bottom edges.

Torn scar low on a trunk, the old crust dark and chewed open in a rough horizontal wound, the fresh resin welling out brighter on the left than the right, a slow thick surge that has already begun sagging downward on the left side into a small new drip-lobe, pale honey where it is freshest and mirror-bright, darkening to near-black at the old crust margin, the wound surface matte and pitted around it, a grit-covered needle stuck into the new wet lobe's surface, the scar filling the lower-left quarter and running off the left and bottom edges.

Lopsided accumulation on a trunk face, three old lobes piled irregularly: the rightmost and lowest is the largest, a flat spread the size of a frond-head, milky and heavily crazed; the middle lobe above it is smaller and offset to the left, dark treacle and smooth; the topmost is a small pale-honey knob far to the right of centre, the fresh run from it tracing a thin line down the right side of the dark middle lobe without joining it, the whole surface dusted with grit, litter banked against the base, filling the right two-thirds and running off the right edge.

Pool on the forest floor where a trunk-base flow spread across an exposed root and dripped beyond it, the pool roughly the size of a large fern frond, its surface skinned and matte, a scatter of needles pressed flat into the skin on the left half, the right half still slightly tacky and dark treacle in colour where it is deepest, pale honey at the thin outer rim, the root cutting across the near edge of the pool and casting a sharp shadow across it, the pool filling the lower-right corner and running off the right and bottom edges.

Welded to the bark where it grew, a fresh flow still moving on the left trunk face — thick as a fern-frond's midrib is wide, heavy enough to sag its own leading edge into a bulging lip, its top skin already wrinkling and matte where it has begun to set while the flanks run pale honey and wet-bright, a single cone-scale pressed flat into the wrinkling crust near the top, the whole mass filling the left quarter of the frame and running off the top and bottom edges.

Welded to the bark where it grew, a fresh flow of pale honey resin bulges outward from a wound halfway up the left trunk, thick as a cone is long, its leading edge sagging and round, the top already wrinkling into a thin skin while the underside stays wet and mirror-bright, one slow lobe spilling down the left side only, a single needle pressed upright into the wrinkling skin at the fattest point, filling the left third of the frame and running off the top and bottom edges

Swelling out of the trunk base on the right side of the frame, a hardened boulder of resin the size of a crouching animal, its outer surface dulled to a matte crust and crazed with internal cracks that run in no pattern, cloudy and milky where old air got trapped in dense white masses, rust-coloured where bark flakes are suspended through it, needle-litter banked against its heavier left flank and a moss frond creeping up that same side, the whole mass running off the right and bottom edges

Welded to the underside of a low branch crossing the upper frame, a bead row of drops at wildly uneven spacing — three crowded almost touching near the left, then a long gap, then one enormous drop twice the size of the others, then two small ones jostling close at the far right — each a dark treacle lens catching daylight from outside, the branch running off both the left and right edges so the bead row spans the full upper width of the frame

Half-buried in the needle-litter at the base of a trunk, a split nodule the size of a large fern-frond's base, its outer crust a dull pitted grey-brown lump dusted with grit and pressed needles, the freshly broken interior face water-clear and pale honey where it is thinnest, deepening to a dark treacle at the thicker interior, one wall of the break gone opaque white like frost at its edge, sitting low in the left-centre of the frame and running off the bottom edge

Lying against an exposed root with needle-litter pressed into its damp underside, a lopsided accumulation of old flows piled unevenly — the largest lobe far left and leaning, a smaller knob of darker and cloudier resin sitting off-centre above it, a third shallow lobe spilling right and trailing to a thin edge, each a different clarity, ranging from near-black at the thickest mass to greenish-clear at the trailing right edge — the whole formation filling the lower-left quarter and running off the left and bottom edges

Welded to a tall trunk where two surfaces meet, a glazed flank of resin coating the full right face of the trunk in one continuous smooth sheet, wet-looking and mirror-bright, pale honey at the thinner upper reaches and deepening to dark treacle where it has built up thickest near the base, a single bubble the size of a large seed-cone's scale stopped halfway up inside it, a twig stuck flat against the surface and sealed under the bright coat, the trunk filling the right half of the frame and running off the top and bottom edges
